title: Rebalancing Tourism in a World Heritage City: The Role of Coastal and Maritime Heritage in Porto, Portugal
content: This study examines whether coastal and maritime heritage can diversify tourism experiences and support a more balanced spatial distribution of visitors in Porto, Portugal. It investigates the determinants of tourists’ intentions to visit coastal experiences and their effects on satisfaction and loyalty, considering the mediating role of visit intentions and moderating effects of age and income. A quantitative survey was conducted with tourists in Porto, Portugal, and 432 responses were collected. The findings show that coastal and maritime tourism motivation and interest most strongly influenced visit intentions and loyalty, while accessibility and information availability had the strongest effect on satisfaction, highlighting the importance of adequate access and information to engage with alternative experiences. Visit intentions also positively affected satisfaction and loyalty, with significant indirect effects supporting its mediating role, whereas age and income did not significantly moderate the relationships. The findings suggest that developing attractive coastal and maritime experiences, supported by adequate accessibility and information, can diversify Porto’s tourism offer and contribute to a more balanced distribution of visitors, reducing concentration in the historic centre while strengthening destination satisfaction and loyalty.
